newsitem.title: USA: Pro-animal protest at Virginia McDonald's; 16 held.
newsitem.headline: Pro-animal protest at Virginia McDonald's; 16 held.

text.p: At least 16 animal rights protesters were arrested Sunday outside a McDonald's fast food restaurant in Crystal City, Virginia, after harassing restaurant patrons and employees, local police said.

The protest, in a business district near Washington, got out of hand after a group of activists entered the restaurant and began throwing trays containing ketchup and other condiments on the floor, a police spokesman said.
Carrying signs that read, "Did your food have a face?," over 100 protesters from around the country had gathered to picket the fast food restaurant and protest its use of paper and meat products.

Arlington County police arrested three protesters inside the restaurant on charges of destruction of property and at least 13 others outside for trespassing when they failed to heed police calls to disband.

Thirty to 40 police officers dressed in riot gear eventually used pepper spray on the crowd and joined forces to drive the protesters back to a hotel where they were holding a grass-roots organizing conference, a police dispatcher said.
Police said they also closed off a two-block section of Jefferson Davis Highway, a major artery in populous Arlington County, for about two hours.
Chris Vellucci, one of the protesters, said the action was planned as a peaceful protest to "show our displeasure with the number of animals they kill every year, the destruction of the rain forest."
